reviews.review: I was ensnared first by paper Harpoon and then by PC Harpoon when it appeared in 1989 or so.  This iteration is an excellent agglomeration of all that is great about the computer version of the game.  I haven't had a chance yet to look around for the scenario/campaign editor (does it exist?), though rumor in the forum has it that the Editor is present but non-functional.  With the enormous number of scenarios included here, I'll be happy for some time. The UI is a little clunky (1990s remember).  The sound effects are just about non-existent, and the music (what there is of it) is crummy. The Platform Data Base is both extensive and accurate.  AI enemies perform IAW historical national naval doctrine of the time. The stress of arranging your assets to deal with as yet undetected threats is palpable.   If you're looking for high grade visuals of ships and aircraft, this game is really not for you.  However...if you're looking for challenging exercises in modern (ok...late 20th Century) naval problem solving, I can recommend this game without reservation.
